title: The Bosphorus Brief — Sunday, 30 August
overview: A quiet Sunday for daily life, but the diplomatic weather is shifting: Turkey summoned Ukraine's ambassador over Black Sea ship attacks, and Erdoğan heads into a Bishkek meeting with Putin this week. Visa news is mostly good for Syrian nationals, while Europe's migration debate keeps intensifying elsewhere.
sections: <parameter name="heading">Black Sea tensions rise, Erdoğan-Putin meeting ahead
body: Turkey summoned Ukraine's ambassador Saturday after attacks this week on a Turkish vessel and a second ship sent to tow it in the Black Sea. Coverage is broad across state, opposition-leaning, and international outlets, suggesting the incident is being taken seriously on all sides, though details of responsibility remain limited to the Foreign Ministry's account. Separately, Erdoğan and Putin are set to meet September 1 in Bishkek on the sidelines of the SCO summit, with Ukraine and Black Sea security on the agenda. For residents, no immediate travel or shipping disruption is reported, but it's worth watching if Black Sea maritime routes see further incidents.
